extracted.intended_audience: hospital and health system leaders, administrators, program directors, and federal health care executives who may apply for or nominate organizations/individuals for AHA awards
extracted.subtask_description: Understanding the eligibility, goals, and evaluative emphases for multiple American Hospital Association awards (leadership awards, program/prize awards, innovation challenges, and federal executive recognitions) so organizations or individuals can prepare nominations/applications that match each award's criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: AHA Leadership Awards (general)
rubrics_metrics.description: AHA Leadership Awards include the Distinguished Service Award, Award of Honor, Justin Ford Kimball Innovators Award, Board of Trustees Award, and Honorary Life Membership.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This category groups multiple leadership recognitions by AHA; each named award will have its own specific criteria (not detailed here). The general emphasis is on leadership contributions to the field of hospitals and health systems.

rubrics_metrics.name: AHA Dick Davidson NOVA Awards
rubrics_metrics.description: Honors effective, collaborative programs focused on improving community health status.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluated on program effectiveness and collaboration and on demonstrable improvements to community health status.

rubrics_metrics.name: American Hospital Association Quest for Quality Prize
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognizes hospital- or system-wide commitment to advancing health by providing exceptional quality, safe, patient- and family-centered, and affordable care that promotes individual and community well-being and adds value to lives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Goals include: raising awareness of the value of hospital/system-wide commitment to advancing health; showcasing successful efforts to develop and promote new and innovative models of care, services and collaboration to provide seamless care; inspiring hospitals and systems to lead and partner with community organizations to improve health status and address health care disparities; and recognizing hospital and system leadership to improve efficiency and effectiveness of care. Applicants should demonstrate organization-wide commitment, innovation, partnership and measurable improvements in quality, safety, access, equity, and value.

rubrics_metrics.name: Circle of Life Award
rubrics_metrics.description: Honors innovative programs in palliative and end-of-life care.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Eligibility: all organizations or groups in the United States that provide palliative and/or end-of-life care. Evaluation emphasis is on innovation in palliative/end-of-life services or programs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Foster G. McGaw Prize for Excellence in Community Service
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognizes health delivery organizations that are exceptionally committed to improving the health and well-being of everyone in their communities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Winners and finalists should demonstrate creative, insightful, and caring approaches to community health — sustained commitment and measurable impact on community health and well-being are central to evaluation. Sponsored by the Baxter International Foundation and the AHA.

rubrics_metrics.name: AHA Rural Hospital Excellence in Innovation Award
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognizes and shares the accomplishments of rural hospitals that exemplify responsiveness, innovation and excellence in developing, implementing and/or sustaining programs and services.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluation focuses on responsiveness to rural community needs, innovative approaches, excellence in execution, and the ability to develop, implement, and sustain programs or services that benefit rural populations.

rubrics_metrics.name: AHA Innovation Challenge (annual competition)
rubrics_metrics.description: An annual competition aimed at accelerating health care innovation, selecting a new topic each year for submissions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Top three proposals receive monetary awards ($100,000, $25,000 and $15,000 respectively) to help innovators bring ideas to life. Previous topics have included social determinants of health and behavioral health. The challenge is sponsored by First American Healthcare Finance. Applicants should align proposals with the selected annual topic, demonstrate innovation potential and feasibility, and propose impact on health care delivery or outcomes. See the Innovation Challenge webpage for detailed submission rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Federal Health Care Executive Award for Excellence
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognizes a senior federal health care executive (uniformed or non-uniformed career commissioned officer 0-6 level or higher/GS-15 level or higher equivalent) whose leadership in directing and orchestrating innovative achievements has distinguished him/her by contributing substantially to the mission of the federal health care system in the 18 months from mid-2023 through 2024.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluation emphasizes senior-level leadership, direction and orchestration of innovative achievements with substantial contribution to the federal health care mission within the specified 18-month performance window.

rubrics_metrics.name: Federal Health Care Executive Special Achievement Award
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognizes a federal career health care executive (uniformed or non-uniformed commissioned officer 0-5 level or lower/GS-14 level or lower equivalent) who has distinguished him/herself through a singular significant achievement or multiple sustained achievements that have enhanced the organization’s mission and/or contributed to the improvement of the federal health care system in the 18 months from mid-2023 through 2024.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluation focuses on significant singular or sustained achievements at career-level positions that enhanced organizational mission or improved the federal health care system within the defined 18-month window.
